frozen_decisions_applied: S4 HTTP required change #1: all 13 canonical v1 routes are now implemented; GET /api/v1/operations/{operation_id} was the last one.

S4 HTTP required change #4/#9: the new kOperationNotFound error code slots into the existing golden matrix (api_v1_error_status()) exactly like every other v1 error code -- no handler invents its own status/token pairing for the new route.

The 'discriminated union across all four domains' design HTTP_API_V1.md's own Section 4.1 (prior revision) proposed verbatim was implemented essentially as described: OperationDomain (the discriminant) + OperationStatusSnapshot (domain + collapsed status), with the actual typed result still fetched via each domain's existing take_*_result() once ready rather than duplicating the 4 result structs into one mega-union -- a smaller, less duplicative implementation of the same idea.

Deliberate scope narrowing, consistent with the OTA/RCP submit-error-mapping precedent already established in this file: the ready-response payload summarizes each domain's most relevant fields rather than replicating every diagnostic field the legacy per-domain GET handlers expose (full scan records, OTA transport error codes, etc.).

operation_result_store_unification.detail: poll_operation_status(request_id) tries network/ota/rcp_update (each already has a get_*_poll_status() method) in turn, then falls back to a non-consuming peek of config's result queue (config never had a poll-status queue at all -- confirmed during this pass that no HTTP/MQTT caller has ever been able to obtain a config request_id to poll with in the first place, since config_patch_handler_v1 responds 200 synchronously with none, so this pre-existing limitation is accurately described, not newly introduced). Dispatch-by-trying-each-domain is safe because all four domains share one global atomic request_id counter (next_operation_request_id()), so a real id can never belong to more than one domain. Tested directly in test_operation_result_store.cpp: unknown id, zero id, and each domain's in-progress -> ready transition (network via scan-queued, OTA via queued, RCP via applying), plus config's result-only visibility.

unified_poll_route.detail: operations_get_handler_v1 parses the operation_id path segment via the new extract_uri_decimal_segment() (mirroring the existing hex-segment parsers' exact-match contract), calls poll_operation_status(), and returns: 404 operation_not_found for unknown ids; 200 {"status":"pending","domain":...} for in-progress; 200 with a domain-specific summary for ready (fetched via the matching take_*_result(), which is destructive -- a second poll of an already-consumed id returns 404, matching the legacy per-domain GET handlers' own existing consume-on-poll semantics exactly, not a new limitation). Registered via register_operations_routes_v1(), wired into register_web_routes_v1() and INV-H010's absence check like every other v1 registration function -- still unregistered by construction in main/app_main.cpp, unchanged from every other S4 HTTP route. Tested end-to-end through a real network scan (post_network_scan -> process_pending -> poll -> ready) and a real OTA start (post_ota_start -> poll while still queued -> pending), not just synthetic OperationResultStore state.

mqtt_command_result_scope_narrowed.status: N/A -- documentation-only clarification, no code change
mqtt_command_result_scope_narrowed.detail: docs/architecture/MQTT_API_V1.md Section 4.1 rewritten to reflect that the shared-infrastructure blocker (OperationResultStore unification) this section previously named is now resolved by this pass, and to name the two MQTT-specific problems that remain: (1) MQTT is push-based (the bridge must decide when to publish, unlike HTTP's pull-based poll) and (2) OperationResultStore's four domains are not uniformly device-scoped the way the command-result topic's path segment requires, and device power commands (the most likely candidate for a pushed result) do not use OperationResultStore at all -- they use the separate CoreCommand/CoreCommandResult mechanism. This is a more precise, smaller remaining problem than 'needs the same unification blocking the HTTP poll', not new deferred work being introduced.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The ready-response payload for GET /api/v1/operations/{operation_id} is a deliberately coarse per-domain summary (ok/status_code plus a handful of fields), not a full replica of every field the legacy per-domain GET handlers (web_handlers_network.cpp/web_handlers_ota.cpp/web_handlers_rcp.cpp) already expose (e.g. full network scan records, OTA transport error codes/TLS diagnostics, HTTP status codes from the OTA download itself).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Consistent with this file's own established precedent (OTA/RCP submit-error mapping, Section 3.5): the golden-matrix/unified-contract philosophy favors a small, stable vocabulary over exposing every internal validation/diagnostic nuance as a top-level v1 field. All four domains' status enums reserve 0 for 'ok', so a generic ok:true/false plus the raw status_code integer is derivable without per-domain enum-to-string mapping duplication, while still exposing the full detail to anyone who needs it via the raw code.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A v1 client cannot distinguish e.g. a specific OTA transport failure reason purely from this endpoint's response; the underlying detail is still available via status_code (and, for now, via the legacy per-domain GET routes, which remain unmodified and fully functional). This is a deliberate, documented scope decision, revisitable later without breaking the response shape (new optional fields could be added).

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: A second poll of an already-ready-and-consumed operation returns 404 operation_not_found, not the golden matrix's '200 completed idempotent replay' framing.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: OperationResultStore's take_*_result() methods are destructive by design (predate this pass, used unchanged) -- this is not a choice made in this pass, it is an existing architectural characteristic of the store being unified. Making the unified poll idempotently re-servable would require either a non-destructive read path for all 4 domains (a larger change to the store's core semantics, affecting the legacy handlers too) or caching the once-fetched result somewhere new. Given this project has no production deployment yet, changing this store-wide is now a legitimate future option, but was judged out of scope for 'unify the domains and build the poll route' specifically.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A client that polls twice after an operation completes will see the result once, then 404 on any subsequent poll -- callers must treat the first ready response as authoritative and final. This matches the legacy handlers' existing behavior exactly, so it is not a regression relative to what a client could already observe via the legacy routes.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: MQTT command-result publishing (topic_v1_device_command_result()'s payload) remains unimplemented.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Narrowed and re-scoped, not newly deferred: the shared OperationResultStore-unification blocker this pass resolves was the ONLY blocker named in the prior two MQTT passes' evidence; what remains (push-timing decision, non-uniform device-scoping across domains, device-power commands using a wholly separate CoreCommandResult mechanism) is genuinely new design surface this pass's HTTP-side work does not resolve.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: No MQTT consumer of the command-result topic exists yet in either direction; purely additive once designed and built.
